schema.op: memory_write | memory_delete | episode_record | task (host-only action that is not a pure edit)
schema.args: the stigmergy call arguments VERBATIM (memory_write: key/description/content; episode_record: its fields incl. memory_keys) so the host session replays op(args) with no interpretation; for task: {instruction}
schema.why: evidence per CLAUDE.md's Evidence Policy — commit hashes, gate runs, measurements
schema.requested: {date, branch, commit} of the work that made the edit necessary

protocol: Producers (sessions without stigmergy tools) APPEND one line per needed edit, in the same commit as the work that makes it necessary. The consumer (a host session with stigmergy) applies each entry and DELETES its line in the SAME commit that applies it — lifting anything durable into a properly-keyed memory first. Applied entries are never kept or struck through; this file shrinks back toward this README line (the handoff-purge rule). Parsers skip op == 'README'. This line is permanent.

args.description: MEASURED 2026-08-23: stacked-alias ORDER decides which label the label DB credits with the body — declare the port-only alias FIRST. A CLASS, not a one-off: 3 pret labels tree-wide still misattributed.
args.content:
When a port-only alias and a pret label are stacked on the same body (two labels, no instruction between them), update_label_db credits the body to whichever label comes SECOND — so the port-only alias must be declared FIRST for the pret label to own its own body. Otherwise the pret label records instr_count=0/has_call=0, faithdiff sees an empty port body, and it reports the routine's ENTIRE call set DROPPED.

Measured 2026-08-23 at src/home/joypad2.asm, master 6c6cc3a vs the rebased link-cable branch, two independent ways. port_defs: with the pret name first, WaitForTextScrollButtonPress = instr_count 0 / has_call 0 while the alias WaitForAPress holds 16; with the alias first, the pret label holds 17 and the alias holds 0. faithdiff on the same label: 4 pret / 0 port calls with everything DROPPED in the first arrangement, 4 pret / 3 port with 2 matched in the second.

PROVENANCE, since it is easy to get backwards: the pret-label-first order is the ORIGINAL and is what master still has. Nobody chose it deliberately. The link-cable branch flipped joypad2.asm's pair in its Stage 3 step-2 commit (pre-rebase 99cb00b) — the same commit that added the CableClub_Run call into that routine, which is what exposed the misattribution — and the rebase onto master preserved the flip.

IT IS A CLASS. Sweeping port_defs for a pret label with an empty body stacked directly above a port-only label that owns it found 4 on master; the link-cable branch fixes 1 (joypad2), leaving 3 OPEN as of 2026-08-23, each reading 0 port calls under faithdiff: LoadScreenTilesFromBuffer1 <- RestoreBattleScreen and SaveScreenTilesToBuffer1 <- SaveBattleScreen (both src/home/tilemap.asm), and InitializeToggleableObjectsFlags <- InitToggleableObjectFlags (src/engine/overworld/toggleable_objects.asm). All three are pre-existing on master and were NOT touched by the link-cable rebase — flagged to the maintainer as out of that task's scope. The fix is a two-line swap per site plus a label-DB rescan; it moves no code.

Do NOT 'fix' a port-only alias that reads as unreached in a stacked pair, and do not reorder a pair to make one look reached: both labels resolve to the same address, so the reached-set membership is a naming artifact of the single-directed-fallthrough-edge model, not behaviour.

why: Two independent measurements per arrangement (port_defs instr_count from each tree's translation.db, and faithdiff on the same label), plus the fallthrough edge tuples from update_label_db.scan_build_graph reversing direction with the order. Provenance from git: the merge base 58c6ddf and origin/master both carry the pret-label-first order; the flip is isolated to the branch's own commit. The class sweep is a port_defs query over adjacent-line defs, run against both trees' DBs.

args.description: RAISED 2026-08-23 1400->2000: test_label_db test_count_delta_direction is a BAND vs the BFS universe, not a budget — decompose before raising
args.content: tools/test_label_db.py::test_count_delta_direction asserts 900 < statically-reached labels < N. N was raised 1400 -> 2000 on 2026-08-23 when the link-cable branch rebased onto master. It guards ONE failure mode: the reachability BFS heading for the whole tree because a terminator rule went lax. Sizing measurements from that day, all of which should be RE-MEASURED rather than quoted: master 6c6cc3a alone = 1362 reached; the rebased link-cable tree = 1409; the BFS universe (labels defined in build-active files) = 4939, so 1409 is 28.5% of it and 2000 is 40%, while a lax terminator would run at ~4900. The +47 was decomposed before the bound moved, per the no-unsupported-confirmations rule: +48 additions, ALL link-cable (serial.asm 9, cable_club.asm 7, link_menu.asm 7, net_hal.asm 6, com_uart.asm 2, net_frame.asm 2, cable_club_npc.asm 1, yes_no.asm 1, plus 13 port-only locals in those same files) and -1 removal (WaitForAPress, see memory joypad2-alias-order-attributes-body-to-pret-label). The bound is expected to be outrun again by ordinary subsystem growth; raising it is legitimate ONLY with the reached-set DIFF against the previous tree, never on the count alone.

why: Reached sets computed on both trees with the same update_label_db.scan_build_graph + BFS that live() uses, then diffed label-by-label; universe size counted from defs whose file is build-active. static_gate PASS after the raise.

ROOT REVIEW BUG WORTH REMEMBERING: the implementer's RX staging pair (rx_stage_pos/len) was cumulative over the connection lifetime - after RX_STAGE_SIZE (2920) total received bytes every in-order segment would be dup-ACK'd forever (link death); fixed pre-commit by recycling the buffer whenever the codec has fully drained it, which is sound ONLY because NetFrame_Tick's .rx_loop drains RX to CF=1 every tick - any datagram/stream transport with per-connection staging must either reset per tick (ipx_dos pattern) or recycle-on-empty (net_ip pattern), never accumulate.
